Definition: Shadrak, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions
BiblicalUsage: Shadrach is the Babylonian name laid on Hananiah, one of Daniel's three companions, when they were set over the affairs of the province of Babylon. When Nebuchadnezzar commanded all to worship the golden image, Shadrach answered that they were not careful to answer the king in the matter, and would not serve his gods. The king cast them into the burning fiery furnace, and then blessed their God, who had sent His angel and delivered His servants.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a new name could not make a new man of Hananiah, because his loyalty belonged to the God of his fathers. Shadrach's answer in the furnace is the pattern for every believer under a king's command: we are not careful to answer, for our God is able to deliver.
